summary: PairUF3Kokkos stores all its spline/coefficient tables in views hard-coded to LMPDeviceType while the class is also instantiated as PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType> for uf3/kk/host, so the host kernels dereference device memory on a GPU build.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.h:88-108 declare 16 members as 'Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> d_coefficients_2b;' ... 'Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT ***[9], LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> dnconstants_3b;' -- LMPDeviceType is hard-coded instead of the class template parameter DeviceType (contrast the correctly written neighbours in the same class, e.g. 'typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d d_cutsq;' at line 78). src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.h:23-25 register 'PairStyle(uf3/kk/host,PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType>)' and src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:tail explicitly instantiates 'template class PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType>;' under '#ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU'. These views are read from KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION bodies dispatched with the class DeviceType, e.g. pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:573-575 'evdwl = constants_2b(interaction_id, start_index, 0);' inside twobody(), called from operator()(TagPairUF3ComputeFullA...).
failure_scenario: GPU build (LMP_KOKKOS_GPU, e.g. CUDA) + 'pair_style uf3/kk/host' (or '-k on ... -pk kokkos ... ' with the /kk/host suffix): the Serial/OpenMP kernel reads constants_2b/d_coefficients_2b, which live in CudaSpace -> Kokkos 'attempt to access inaccessible memory space' abort or a segfault. On a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType so the bug is invisible.
suggested_fix: Replace LMPDeviceType with the class template parameter (use 'typename KKDevice<DeviceType>::value' or 'DeviceType') in all of pair_uf3_kokkos.h:88-108, or drop the /kk/host registration and the LMPHostType instantiation.

summary: NPairTrimKokkos's constructor never sets execution_space, so it keeps NPair's default 'Host' and trim_to_kokkos() syncs x to the wrong space before reading the DeviceType view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:26-27 'template<class DeviceType>\nNPairTrimKokkos<DeviceType>::NPairTrimKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : NPair(lmp) {}' -- no assignment. src/npair.cpp:44 sets 'execution_space = Host;'. The sibling builders do set it: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:31-34 'NPairHalffullKokkos<...>::NPairHalffullKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : NPair(lmp) { atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom; execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space; }' and src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:28. The stale value is then used at src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:56-57 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();\n  atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);'.
failure_scenario: GPU build with a trimmed Kokkos neighbor list (neighbor list request with a custom cutoff, e.g. a compute/fix that asks for a shorter cutoff list, so NPairTrimKokkos<LMPDeviceType> is used): sync(Host,X_MASK) refreshes the legacy host mirror instead of the device view, so if x was last written on the host the device view d_x is stale and the trimmed list is built from out-of-date coordinates -> wrong/missing neighbors.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom; execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;' to the NPairTrimKokkos constructor, matching npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:31-34.

summary: compute() reads neighflag before the host_flag branch, but init_style() returns early on the host path without ever assigning neighflag, so the /kk/host variant reads an uninitialized member.
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'pair_style pod/kk/host': neighflag holds indeterminate garbage; if it happens to equal FULL, no_virial_fdotr_compute is set to 1 and the global virial from the fdotr accumulation is dropped -> wrong pressure. Reading an uninitialized int is also UB flagged by MSan/valgrind.
suggested_fix: Initialize neighflag in the constructor (e.g. 'neighflag = HALF;') and/or move the 'if (host_flag)' branch in compute() above the 'if (neighflag == FULL)' test, as pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp does.

summary: remove_deform_bias_all_kk() captures the x view and syncs X before calling DomainKokkos::x2lamda(), which always converts on the device and marks only the device side modified, so the host instantiation computes the bias from unconverted (box, not lamda) coordinates.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:175-192:
  'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK);'
  'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'
  ...
  'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);'
  ...
  'Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias >(0,nlocal),*this);'
src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:672-687 shows x2lamda(int) is device-only: 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); ... atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);'. The correct ordering is used in the sibling style, src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_profile_kokkos.cpp:82-91: 'if (triclinic) domain->x2lamda(nlocal);' FIRST, then 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, X_MASK | MASK_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();', with the comment 'DomainKokkos does the conversions with device kernels that sync X themselves'.
failure_scenario: GPU build, triclinic box, 'fix deform' + 'compute temp/deform/kk/host' (e.g. via 'fix nvt/sllod/kk/host' or 'package kokkos ... ' running the thermostat on the host): the host kernel at line 203 reads the host mirror of x, which x2lamda never touched, so vbiasall is built from box coordinates instead of lamda coordinates -> wrong streaming-velocity bias, wrong temperature and wrong thermostatting. On a CPU-only build view<DeviceType>() and view_device() are the same view, so the bug is invisible.
suggested_fix: Move 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' above the sync/view-capture block (and re-sync X for execution_space after it), mirroring compute_temp_profile_kokkos.cpp:82-91.

summary: ComputeGaussianGridLocalKokkos::compute_local() returns immediately when host_flag is set, so the /kk/host variant silently produces no grid data at all.
failure_scenario: Any build where execution_space is HostKK -- i.e. a CPU-only Kokkos build (ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<LMPHostType>::space == HostKK, kokkos_type.h:220-223) or a GPU build with the /kk/host suffix: 'compute gaussian/grid/local/kk' returns an all-zero (or stale) local array to whatever dumps or fixes read it, with no error.
suggested_fix: Call 'ComputeGaussianGridLocal::compute_local(); return;' in the host branch (and set invoked_local), or refuse the host instantiation with a clear error message.

summary: The host fallback of ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::compute_local() calls ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(), a method that class does not define, so it resolves to the empty virtual Compute::compute_array() and nothing is computed.
failure_scenario: CPU-only Kokkos build, or GPU build with 'compute sna/grid/local/kk/host': the local array is never filled; dumps/fixes reading it get zeros with no error or warning.
suggested_fix: Call 'ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local();' instead of compute_array() in the host branch.

summary: The host/device dispatch for compute_X is short-circuited with '|| 1', so the GPU team-based path is dead code and the device instantiation always runs the CPU-style parallel_scan.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:343 'if (execution_space == HostKK || 1) { // CPU' followed by the team-based branch at line 354 '} else { // GPU, use teams'. The matching dispatch for compute_H at line ~ (same file) is written without the '|| 1'.
failure_scenario: GPU build with fix qeq/reacxff style acks2: the team/vector-length tuned kernel (num_teams/atoms_per_team/vector_length at lines 357-362) is never launched; the flat parallel_scan is used instead. Not a wrong-answer bug, but the whole else-branch is unreachable code that a compiler may warn about and that hides whether the device path still works.
suggested_fix: Either delete the unreachable GPU branch or remove the '|| 1' and fix whatever made it necessary; add a comment if the device path is intentionally disabled.

summary: GetMaxNeighs() dispatches a bare lambda parallel_reduce with no execution space, so it always runs on Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace (LMPDeviceType) even when called with a host neighbor list from a /kk/host pair style on a GPU build.
failure_scenario: GPU build with a GPU present (ngpus > 0) running a host pair style, e.g. '-k on g 1 -sf kk' with 'pair_style lj/cut/kk/host': pair_kokkos.h:900-903 auto-enables neigh_thread when ngpus is set and inum <= 16000, so GetMaxNeighs() is reached and a CUDA/HIP kernel dereferences HostSpace views -> Kokkos 'attempt to access inaccessible memory space' abort (or garbage/crash).
suggested_fix: Give the reduction an explicit policy tied to the list's device type, e.g. 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::RangePolicy<typename NeighStyle::device_type>(0,inum), ...)', or reuse the existing FindMaxNumNeighs<DeviceType> functor.
